newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's IFI confirms control of Juventus.
newsitem.headline: Italy's IFI confirms control of Juventus.

text.p: The Agnelli family holding company IFI confirmed on Wednesday that it held directly some 99.6 percent of the share capital of one of Italy's leading soccer teams Juventus FC SpA.

In an IFI statement, along with its 1996 financial results, the group said it had bought a 42.2 percent stake in Juventus from Sisport Fiat, part of the Fiat empire, for 23 billion lire in the first months of this year, and had also underwritten a capital increase of 16.4 billion lire.
After these operations, IFI said it now controlled 99.6 percent of the share capital of Juventus, who currently hold the European Cup and are leaders of Italy's Serie A.

IFI is controlled by the Agnelli family, and itself has a controlling stake in fellow holding company IFIL. IFI and IFIL together are the largest shareholders in Fiat with a combined 32.5 percent stake.

In an interview last month, Juventus honorary president Umberto Agnelli said the Turin-based club had no immediate intention of seeking a stock market listing. Some Italian clubs such as AC Milan and Bologna have already expressed an interest in a stock market flotation.
IFI said that its 1996 net consolidated profits were in line with the 411 billion lire profit seen in 1995.
